title: Equation-Solving Attacks on Ciminion
summary: Ciminion’s truncated outputs make trivial meet-in-the-middle linearization difficult; whether equation-solving methods can exploit the resulting systems remains open.

formal_statement.body: For Ciminion, whose truncated output means that part of each output changes while remaining secret, each collected equation introduces additional secret variables, making a meet-in-the-middle-style trivial linearization difficult. It remains unresolved whether equation-solving attacks, including Gröbner-basis methods and other algebraic techniques, can exploit the resulting systems, and whether the equation systems generated after a few rounds contain exploitable structure such as sparse equations.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of Ciminion’s truncated-output equation systems, contrasted with meet-in-the-middle linearization.
parameters: Number of collected equations: each equation adds secret variables to the system
Number of rounds: determines the equation systems examined for exploitable structure
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether Gröbner-basis or other algebraic equation-solving attacks can exploit the resulting systems, including special few-round structure such as sparse equations.

citations.label: Ciminion: Symmetric Encryption Based on Toffoli-Gates over Large Finite Fields

progress.summary: The source argues that truncation and newly introduced secret variables obstruct trivial meet-in-the-middle linearization. It leaves open whether equation-solving methods can exploit special structure, such as sparse equations, in few-round systems.
citation_labels: Christoph Dobraunig et al., Ciminion: Symmetric Encryption Based on Toffoli-Gates over Large Finite Fields
